# Isleta 1.2.0
The island holds two things at once, Clock timers count down beside the notch, and hovering an open island reveals a row for switching between everything Isleta is holding.
## New
- **Clock timers appear in the island.** Start a timer in Clock and the countdown rides in the sliver beside the notch, drawn as Clock's own ring — orange while it runs, grey while it is paused. No permission is asked for and nothing is polled while no timer exists. - **Music and a timer at the same time.** Music takes the left of the notch and a countdown the right, whichever of the two is holding the island open. - **Hover an open island for the switcher.** A row of chips appears along the bottom listing everything Isleta is currently holding. Click one to bring it to the front — it stays there for half a minute, longer than a swipe holds it. Move the pointer away and the row goes. - **Recent notifications, on the ✉ chip.** The last twenty that came through, including the ones that arrived while you were reading another and never made it to the island. Five fit; the rest are counted underneath. Held in memory only — never written to disk, never in an exported log, gone when Isleta quits. - **The menu bar icon can be hidden**, in Settings › General. Your own shortcut still opens the island from any app, and the ⚙ chip in the switcher row is the way back into Settings.
## Improved
- **A finished timer does not take over the island.** It shows itself beside the notch the way a volume change does, and Clock's own notification is left to be the thing you click. - **Long countdowns fit the sliver.** An hour and four minutes reads `1h04` rather than being clipped to `4:` above an ellipsis. - **The island grows and settles for the switcher row** on one spring, in both directions, instead of snapping it in and out.
## Requirements
macOS 26 or later, on Apple Silicon. Displays with a real notch get the island; a Mac with none gets a synthesized island on the primary display.
## Known limitations
- **A timer started by Siri, Shortcuts or Control Center can take a few seconds to appear.** One started by hand in Clock is there immediately; macOS gives no signal for the others, and Isleta will not poll for them. - **Brightness has no HUD.** macOS offers no public way to read display brightness on Apple Silicon. - **Apple's own HUDs are not replaced.** Isleta shows its own alongside them. - **The island sits above Mission Control.** In a real notch it covers nothing; a synthesized island can cover the centre of the space labels. - **A burst of notifications opens the island once for each.** The ✉ chip is where the ones you missed go; grouping them as they arrive is a later release's job. - **The hover target is the notch itself** — 185×32 points, and easy to overshoot. - **Playing music costs more than it should.** About 7.7% CPU against an internal 4% budget for an animating island, and a 250–290 MB footprint against a 60 MB one. It is not a leak: resident memory is flat and plateaus rather than climbing. Idle is unaffected — around 0.04% with nothing on stage, and a timer counting down does not measurably change that. - **Not on the Mac App Store.** Signed with a Developer ID, notarized by Apple, and updated through Sparkle.

# Isleta 1.1.2
Notifications no longer disappear when you click somewhere else.
## Fixed
- **A notification stays long enough to read.** Clicking elsewhere still closes an island *you* opened, but no longer one that opened itself — the click that carried on whatever you were doing was taking the message away first. Escape, clicking the island, or swiping it up still close it.
## Requirements
macOS 26 or later, on Apple Silicon. Displays with a real notch get the island; a Mac with none gets a synthesized island on the primary display.
## Known limitations
- **Brightness has no HUD.** macOS offers no public way to read display brightness on Apple Silicon. - **Apple's own HUDs are not replaced.** Isleta shows its own alongside them. - **The island sits above Mission Control.** In a real notch it covers nothing; a synthesized island can cover the centre of the space labels. - **A burst of notifications opens the island once for each.** Grouping them is a later release's job. - **The hover target is the notch itself** — 185×32 points, and easy to overshoot. - **Playing music costs about 0.4% CPU**, against an internal 0.3% budget. Everything else is inside budget. - **Not on the Mac App Store.** Signed with a Developer ID, notarized by Apple, and updated through Sparkle.

# Isleta 1.1.1
A fix for 1.1.0: the General page in Settings could not be clicked.
## Improved
- **The Notifications row says where you stand in three words** — "Granted." or "Not granted yet." — instead of a paragraph restating the description directly above it.
## Fixed
- **General could not be clicked in Settings.** 1.1.0 put a blur behind the sidebar's icon and version number so the page names pass behind them when the list scrolls. It reached 28 points too far down, over the first row, where it quietly swallowed clicks — so anyone who navigated to another page could not get back to General.
## Requirements
